stories.headline: OpenAI Missed Internal Revenue and 1B Weekly User Target, CFO Worried About Paying Compute Contracts

key_facts.fact: OpenAI missed an internal goal of reaching 1 billion weekly active ChatGPT users by the end of 2025
key_facts.excerpt: A target to hit 1 billion weekly active users by the end of 2025.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI missed its annual revenue target for ChatGPT last year and multiple monthly revenue targets in early 2026, as Anthropic surged in enterprise markets
key_facts.excerpt: Its annual revenue target for ChatGPT last year. Multiple monthly revenue targets this year, as Anthropic has surged ahead in the enterprise markets.

key_facts.fact: CFO Sarah Friar told company leaders she is worried OpenAI might not be able to pay for future computing contracts if revenue doesn't grow fast enough
key_facts.excerpt: Sarah Friar, the company's CFO has 'told other company leaders that she is worried the company might not be able to pay for future computing contracts if revenue doesn't grow fast enough.'

key_facts.fact: Friar has also expressed reservations about OpenAI's plans to go public by the end of 2026

stories.headline: Microsoft and OpenAI Overhaul Deal: End Exclusivity, Drop AGI Clause, Open Multi-Cloud Access

key_facts.fact: OpenAI can now serve all products across any cloud provider including AWS and Google Cloud, ending Microsoft's exclusivity as sole cloud provider
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI, critically, can now serve all of its products to customers on any cloud provider — including Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud — ending the exclusivity that had been a cornerstone of the original deal.

key_facts.fact: The controversial AGI clause has been eliminated; Microsoft now retains a non-exclusive IP license through a fixed date of 2032, regardless of technology progress
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft retains a license to OpenAI's intellectual property for models and products through 2032, but that license is now explicitly non-exclusive.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft will no longer pay any revenue share to OpenAI; OpenAI continues paying Microsoft 20% through 2030, now subject to a total cap
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft will no longer pay any revenue share to OpenAI when customers access OpenAI models through Azure. OpenAI, meanwhile, will continue paying a revenue share to Microsoft through 2030 — at the same 20 percent rate — but that obligation is now subject to a total cap.

key_facts.fact: The restructuring was driven by Amazon's $50B investment in OpenAI and $100B AWS cloud commitment, which conflicted with the original Microsoft exclusivity
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI announced that Amazon would invest up to $50 billion in the company — $15 billion upfront, with another $35 billion to follow... committed to making AWS the exclusive third-party distribution provider for Frontier

key_facts.fact: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said OpenAI's models will be available on Bedrock 'in the coming weeks' alongside the Stateful Runtime Environment
key_facts.excerpt: We're excited to make OpenAI's models available directly to customers on Bedrock in the coming weeks, alongside the upcoming Stateful Runtime Environment

key_facts.fact: Microsoft retains approximately 27% ownership of OpenAI's for-profit entity and reported $7.5B in revenue from its OpenAI investment in a single quarter
key_facts.excerpt: it retains approximately 27 percent ownership of OpenAI's for-profit entity... Last quarter alone, Microsoft reported $7.5 billion in revenue from its OpenAI investment in a single quarter

stories.headline: Ex-DeepMind's David Silver Raises Record $1.1B Seed at $5.1B Valuation for Ineffable Intelligence

key_facts.fact: Ineffable Intelligence, founded by ex-Google DeepMind Principal Scientist David Silver (creator of AlphaGo), raised $1.1B in seed funding at a $5.1B valuation
key_facts.excerpt: Ineffable Intelligence, founded by renowned AI researcher David Silver, secured approximately $1.1 billion in seed funding, one of the largest early-stage financings ever recorded. The round values the company at roughly $5.1 billion

key_facts.fact: The round includes participation from Nvidia, Google, Sequoia, and the UK Sovereign AI Fund, making it one of the largest seed rounds ever recorded
key_facts.excerpt: includes participation from major global investors, including Nvidia and Google, as well as leading venture capital firms

key_facts.fact: The London-based company is focused on developing 'superlearner' AI systems based on reinforcement learning that learn autonomously through experience, without relying on human-generated data
key_facts.excerpt: focused on developing advanced AI systems based on reinforcement learning rather than traditional large language models. Silver... is pursuing a 'superlearner' approach in which AI systems learn autonomously through experience instead of relying on human-generated data.

key_facts.fact: The company was founded in late 2025 and is headquartered in London, marking a milestone for Europe's AI ecosystem
key_facts.excerpt: launched in late 2025 and headquartered in London... The record-setting round also marks a milestone for Europe's technology ecosystem

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced a collaboration with Ineffable Intelligence, with more details to come
key_facts.excerpt: Congrats to @IneffableLabs on today's launch out of stealth. Super excited on our collaboration with their team. More details to come soon.

stories.headline: Xiaomi Open-Sources MiMo-V2.5 Trillion-Parameter Models Under MIT License, Rivals Frontier Models

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi released MiMo-V2.5-Pro (1.02T total params, 42B active) and MiMo-V2.5 (310B total params, 15B active) under the MIT License with 1M context window
key_facts.excerpt: By combining a massive 310B-parameter architecture with a highly efficient 'active' footprint and a native 1-million-token context window

key_facts.fact: MiMo-V2.5-Pro leads the open-source field with 63.8% success rate on ClawEval benchmarks, using ~70K tokens per trajectory — 40-60% fewer tokens than Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4
key_facts.excerpt: the Pro model leads the open-source field with a 63.8% success rate, consuming only ~70K tokens per trajectory. This is roughly 40–60% fewer tokens than those required by Anthropic Claude Opus 4.6, Google Gemini 3.1 Pro, and OpenAI GPT-5.4

key_facts.fact: The Pro model achieved 1581 on GDPVal-AA (Elo) benchmark, surpassing Kimi K2.6 and GLM 5.1
key_facts.excerpt: On the GDPVal-AA (Elo) benchmark, the Pro model achieved a score of 1581, surpassing competitors like Kimi K2.6 and GLM 5.1.

key_facts.fact: V2.5-Pro autonomously implemented a complete SysY compiler in Rust in 4.3 hours (672 tool calls, 233/233 on test suites) and built an 8,192-line video editor in 11.5 hours
key_facts.excerpt: SysY Compiler in Rust: The model implemented a complete compiler from scratch—including lexer, parser, and RISC-V assembly backend—in 4.3 hours. Spanning 672 tool calls, the model achieved a perfect 233/233 score

key_facts.fact: API pricing: Pro at $1.00/M input tokens, $3.00/M output (≤256K context); base model at $0.40/M input, $2.00/M output, making them among the cheapest frontier-class models
key_facts.excerpt: the high-performance MiMo-V2.5-Pro is priced at $1.00 per million input tokens... and $3.00 for output within context windows up to 256K

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi is offering developers and creators 100 trillion free tokens to build with the models
key_facts.excerpt: we're giving devs & creators 100T tokens on us. Go build

stories.headline: OpenAI Releases Symphony, Open-Source Agent Orchestrator That Turns Issue Trackers Into Coding Agent Control Planes

key_facts.fact: Symphony is an open-source orchestration layer that connects project management tools like Linear to Codex agents, assigning a dedicated agent workspace to each open issue
key_facts.excerpt: Symphony is an orchestration layer that turns a project-management board such as Linear into a control plane for coding agents. Each open task is assigned a dedicated agent workspace, agents run continuously, and engineers review the output.

key_facts.fact: Some OpenAI teams saw a 500% increase in landed pull requests during the first three weeks of using Symphony
key_facts.excerpt: Some teams at OpenAI saw a 500% increase in landed pull requests during the first three weeks of using Symphony.

key_facts.fact: The repo has already accumulated 15,500 stars on GitHub since its quiet launch last month
key_facts.excerpt: We quietly launched the Symphony repo on Github last month, and it's already accumulated 15.5k stars!

key_facts.fact: OpenAI built an internal productivity tool with no human-written code, using the Symphony approach where every open issue gets a Codex agent
key_facts.excerpt: Six months ago, while working on an internal productivity tool, our team made a controversial (at the time) decision: we'd build our repo with no human-written code.

key_facts.fact: Symphony is positioned as a reference implementation, not a standalone product; OpenAI encourages teams to fork and rebuild it for their own needs
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI does not plan to maintain Symphony as a standalone product, treating it as a reference implementation that other teams can study, fork, or rebuild.

stories.headline: GitHub Copilot Moving to Usage-Based Billing on June 1, Replacing Premium Requests With AI Credits

key_facts.fact: All GitHub Copilot plans will transition to usage-based billing on June 1, 2026, replacing premium request units with GitHub AI Credits based on token consumption
key_facts.excerpt: all GitHub Copilot plans will transition to usage-based billing on June 1, 2026. Instead of counting premium requests, every Copilot plan will include a monthly allotment of GitHub AI Credits

key_facts.fact: Base plan pricing remains unchanged: Pro $10/month, Pro+ $39/month, Business $19/user/month, Enterprise $39/user/month, with equivalent monthly AI Credits included
key_facts.excerpt: Copilot Pro remains $10/month, Pro+ remains $39/month, Business remains $19/user/month, and Enterprise remains $39/user/month.

key_facts.fact: GitHub cited that the current premium request model is no longer sustainable as Copilot evolved from an in-editor assistant into an agentic platform with much higher compute demands
key_facts.excerpt: It has evolved from an in-editor assistant into an agentic platform capable of running long, multi-step coding sessions... the current premium request model is no longer sustainable.

key_facts.fact: Code completions and Next Edit suggestions remain included in all plans and do not consume AI Credits; fallback experiences to lower-cost models will no longer be available
key_facts.excerpt: Code completions and Next Edit suggestions remain included in all plans and do not consume AI Credits. Fallback experiences will no longer be available.

key_facts.fact: Annual Pro and Pro+ subscribers are grandfathered into the existing plan until expiration, but model multipliers increase on June 1 — Claude Opus 4.7 goes from 7.5x to 27x
key_facts.excerpt: Users on annual Pro or Pro+ plans will remain on their existing plan with premium request-based pricing until their plan expires. Model multipliers will increase on June 1

key_facts.fact: Enterprise customers get promotional credits for June-August: Business $30/month, Enterprise $70/month in AI Credits, with new pooled usage across organizations
key_facts.excerpt: existing Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise customers will automatically receive promotional included usage for June, July, and August: Copilot Business: $30 in monthly AI Credits, Copilot Enterprise: $70 in monthly AI Credits

stories.headline: 600+ Google Employees Including DeepMind Staff Demand Pichai Bar Pentagon From Using AI on Classified Work

key_facts.fact: More than 600 Google employees signed an open letter to CEO Sundar Pichai demanding he bar the Pentagon from using Google's AI for classified work
key_facts.excerpt: More than 600 Google employees have called on the company to reject a potential deal with the Pentagon that would allow its artificial intelligence to be used in secret military operations

key_facts.fact: Signers span Google DeepMind, Cloud and other divisions, including more than 20 directors, senior directors and vice presidents
key_facts.excerpt: The letter, signed by staff across Google DeepMind, Cloud and other divisions... has been signed openly by more than 20 directors, senior directors and vice presidents.

key_facts.fact: Google reportedly signed a deal allowing the US DOD to use Google's AI for 'any lawful government purpose'; the Pentagon pushed for broader 'all lawful uses' wording
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon, however, has pushed for broader 'all lawful uses' wording, arguing it is necessary to maintain operational flexibility.

key_facts.fact: The protest is the largest internal Google dissent in years, exceeding the anti-Israel protests and echoing the 2018 Project Maven controversy that led Google to withdraw from a drone footage AI program
key_facts.excerpt: draws comparisons to a previous employee protest in 2018 that led Google to withdraw from Project Maven, a Pentagon initiative using AI to analyse drone footage

key_facts.fact: Google has proposed contractual language preventing Gemini from being used for domestic mass surveillance or autonomous weapons without human control, but employees say safeguards would be hard to enforce
key_facts.excerpt: Google has proposed contractual language that would prevent Gemini from being used for domestic mass surveillance or autonomous weapons without appropriate human control... Employees say such safeguards would be difficult to enforce
